provenance.note: The single-signature conversation is written inline in `credentials.test.ts`, so each step is driven through the reference's own `Ipex` method with the same arguments in the same order. The group rounds live in `multisig-utils.ts`, which is **transpiled in memory** by the reference's own pinned TypeScript and evaluated with a module shim, as the `client-multisig-inception` generator does. Nothing is written into the submodule. The clock and the agent's key are pinned; the local member is the reference's own `mockGetAID`. `PUBLIC TEST MATERIAL`: the passcode and sealed salt are the pinned tests' own.

declarations.grant_multisig: export async function grantMultisig( client: SignifyClient, aid: HabState, otherMembersAIDs: HabState[], multisigAID: HabState, recipientAID: HabState, credential: any, timestamp: string, isInitiator: boolean = false ): Promise<string> { if (!isInitiator) await waitAndMarkNotification(client, '/multisig/exn'); const [grant, sigs, end] = await client.ipex().grant({ senderName: multisigAID.name, acdc: new Serder(credential.sad), anc: new Serder(credential.anc), iss: new Serder(credential.iss), recipient: recipientAID.prefix, datetime: timestamp, }); await client .ipex() .submitGrant(multisigAID.name, grant, sigs, end, [recipientAID.prefix]); const mstate = multisigAID.state; const seal = [ 'SealEvent', { i: multisigAID.prefix, s: mstate['ee']['s'], d: mstate['ee']['d'] }, ]; const sigers = sigs.map((sig) => new signify.Siger({ qb64: sig })); const gims = signify.d(signify.messagize(grant, sigers, seal)); let atc = gims.substring(grant.size); atc += end; const gembeds = { exn: [grant, atc], }; const recp = otherMembersAIDs.map((aid) => aid.prefix); await client .exchanges() .send( aid.name, 'multisig', aid, '/multisig/exn', { gid: multisigAID.prefix }, gembeds, recp ); return grant.said; }
declarations.admit_multisig: export async function admitMultisig( client: SignifyClient, aid: HabState, otherMembersAIDs: HabState[], multisigAID: HabState, recipientAID: HabState, timestamp: string, isInitiator: boolean = false // numGrantMsgs: number ): Promise<string> { if (!isInitiator) await waitAndMarkNotification(client, '/multisig/exn'); const grantMsgSaid = await waitAndMarkNotification( client, '/exn/ipex/grant' ); const [admit, sigs, end] = await client.ipex().admit({ senderName: multisigAID.name, message: '', grantSaid: grantMsgSaid, recipient: recipientAID.prefix, datetime: timestamp, }); await client .ipex() .submitAdmit(multisigAID.name, admit, sigs, end, [recipientAID.prefix]); const mstate = multisigAID.state; const seal = [ 'SealEvent', { i: multisigAID.prefix, s: mstate['ee']['s'], d: mstate['ee']['d'] }, ]; const sigers = sigs.map((sig: string) => new signify.Siger({ qb64: sig })); const ims = signify.d(signify.messagize(admit, sigers, seal)); let atc = ims.substring(admit.size); atc += end; const gembeds = { exn: [admit, atc], }; const recp = otherMembersAIDs.map((aid) => aid.prefix); await client .exchanges() .send( aid.name, 'multisig', aid, '/multisig/exn', { gid: multisigAID.prefix }, gembeds, recp ); return admit.said; }
declarations.multisig_admit_credential: async function multisigAdmitCredential( client: SignifyClient, groupName: string, memberAlias: string, grantSaid: string, issuerPrefix: string, recipients: string[], isInitiator: boolean = false ): Promise<{ op: Operation; admitSaid: string }> { const mHab = await client.identifiers().get(memberAlias); const gHab = await client.identifiers().get(groupName); if (!isInitiator) await waitAndMarkNotification(client, '/multisig/exn'); const [admit, sigs, end] = await client.ipex().admit({ senderName: groupName, message: '', grantSaid: grantSaid, recipient: issuerPrefix, datetime: TIME, }); const op = await client .ipex() .submitAdmit(groupName, admit, sigs, end, [issuerPrefix]); const mstate = gHab['state']; const seal = [ 'SealEvent', { i: gHab['prefix'], s: mstate['ee']['s'], d: mstate['ee']['d'] }, ]; const sigers = sigs.map((sig: any) => new signify.Siger({ qb64: sig })); const ims = signify.d(signify.messagize(admit, sigers, seal)); let atc = ims.substring(admit.size); atc += end; const gembeds = { exn: [admit, atc], }; await client .exchanges() .send( mHab.name, 'multisig', mHab, '/multisig/exn', { gid: gHab['prefix'] }, gembeds, recipients ); return { op, admitSaid: admit.said }; }

'', }; let atc = args.ancAttachment; if (atc === undefined) { const keeper = this.client.manager!.get(hab); const sigs = await keeper.sign(b(args.anc.raw)); const sigers = sigs.map((sig: string) => new Siger({ qb64: sig })); const ims = d(messagize(args.anc, sigers)); atc = ims.substring(args.anc.size); } const acdcAtc = args.acdcAttachment === undefined ? d(serializeACDCAttachment(args.iss)) : args.acdcAttachment; const issAtc = args.issAttachment === undefined ? d(serializeIssExnAttachment(args.anc)) : args.issAttachment; const embeds: Record<string, [Serder, string]> = { acdc: [args.acdc, acdcAtc], iss: [args.iss, issAtc], anc: [args.anc, atc], }; return this.client .exchanges() .createExchangeMessage( hab, '/ipex/grant', data, embeds, args.recipient, args.datetime, args.agreeSaid ); }

notes.waiter: `return notes[notes.length - 1]?.a.d ?? '';` — marks every match read, returns the last, and yields the empty string when a notification names no message
notes.stamp: an IPEX message's SAID covers its `dt`, so two members must agree on a timestamp to build one message

pinned_confirmations.note: an apply and an agree embed nothing, an offer embeds `acdc` alone, and a grant embeds `{acdc, iss, anc}`. A group announces the whole message under `exn` on `/multisig/exn`.

a_group_round_agrees_only_on_a_shared_cl.declaration: `datetime: timestamp` on both halves; `const TIME = createTimestamp()` in the holder test
a_group_round_agrees_only_on_a_shared_cl.note: an IPEX message's SAID covers its `dt`. Both helpers take the stamp as a parameter and the holder test reads one module-level constant, so the members agree only because one process handed both the same value. One second apart they build different messages, the group never reaches its threshold on either, and neither call fails. The reference's own equality assertion is the only thing that would notice, and it lives inside the process that made them equal.
a_group_round_agrees_only_on_a_shared_cl.rust_decision: `accept_admittance` takes no timestamp at all: the stamp, the recipient, the text, and the grant being acknowledged are read out of the proposal, and the SAID this member derives is compared with the one it was shown. `accept_disclosure` does the same.

a_joining_member_never_reads_the_proposa.note: the same shape the `client-multisig-credentials` fixture pinned for the transaction rounds, in all three group IPEX helpers. Driven across six group rounds, not one fetches a group request.
a_joining_member_never_reads_the_proposa.rust_decision: the proposed message is read out of the `/multisig/exn` proposal and rebuilt from its own fields.

a_notification_need_not_name_a_message.note: the waiter yields the empty string when a notification carries no `a.d`, and `admitMultisig` passes it straight into `grantSaid`. Driven: the admit is built and posted with an empty `p`, acknowledging nothing, with no error. The inline step in `credentials.test.ts` guards the same value with `assert(grantNotification.a.d)` first; the helper beside it does not.
a_notification_need_not_name_a_message.rust_decision: `Presentation::read` requires the notification to name a SAID and refuses with `UnaddressedNotification`, so no step can be built from a notification that announces nothing.

only_the_last_notification_survives.note: `waitAndMarkNotification` marks every matching notification read and returns only the last one's SAID. A holder group admitting from a multisig issuer receives one grant per issuer member; it answers one and silently marks the rest read. The parameter that would have said how many to expect — `numGrantMsgs: number` — is still in the tree, commented out.
only_the_last_notification_survives.rust_decision: `Presentation::waiting` returns every unread notification on the route, and the caller answers each.

a_grant_assembles_its_attachments_three_.note: the presentation grant passes all three attachments, the issuance grant passes the anchor's only, and `multisig-holder.test.ts` passes none. Passing none reaches the branch that signs `args.anc.raw` with the *sender's* keeper — correct only when the sender is the issuer, and reached in the tree where it is not.
a_grant_assembles_its_attachments_three_.rust_decision: the credentials endpoint refused that branch: a `Disclosure` carries its own three attachments, derived from the issuance artifacts or read off the credential. `presentation::disclosure_of` assembles them from a credential in hand, and re-serializes each of the three events to check its bytes still reproduce the SAID that names it.

an_announcement_names_only_the_group.declaration: export type MultisigExnExchange = ExchangeResourceV1 & { exn: ExnV1 & { r: typeof MULTISIG_EXN_ROUTE; e: { exn: ExnV1; d?: string; }; a: { gid: string; [key: string]: unknown; }; }; };
an_announcement_names_only_the_group.recipients_source: const recipients = members.signing .map((m: { aid: string }) => m.aid) .filter((aid: string) => aid !== leaderHab.prefix);
an_announcement_names_only_the_group.note: a `/multisig/exn` proposal carries `{ gid }` and nothing else — `MultisigExnExchange` declares no `smids` — and both group IPEX helpers take the peers as an argument, so a joining member is told who to answer by its caller rather than by the message. Where the reference's own tests derive the members themselves (`multisigIssue`, `multisigRevoke`) they ask the agent's members endpoint for `signing[].aid`; the group record's `keys` are the members' signing keys and never stand in for them.
an_announcement_names_only_the_group.rust_decision: the IPEX rounds announce `smids` and `rmids` exactly as the six event rounds do, so a joining member reads its peers from the proposal it was shown; a proposal that names nobody — the reference's — is answered by `identifiers().members(group)`, never by the record's keys. The classifier accepts both shapes on `/multisig/exn`.
